_doc: Grimmaul, Blacksmith of the Ninth Forge (Brimstone Foundry). Pool 'grimmaul' (shop ids: blacksmith, forge). once=true entries are story beats (one per Basecamp visit), the rest is repeatable chatter.

lines.text: Another Sinbound. The Font spat you out still smoking.
Grimmaul. Ninth Forge. I make the things that make angels into ash.

choices.text: What do you want for them?

lines.label: price
lines.text: Souls. Steel drinks them. Bring me souls, leave sharper.

lines.label: proud
lines.text: Hah. The last one said that too. He is a stain on the Ashen Plain now.
Come back when you are smarter. Or deader. Same thing, around here.
Burnt hair, broken pride. I have seen worse. Usually on my anvil.
Dying is no shame, Sinbound. Dying the same way twice, that is shame.
You brought down the Herald. Whole camp felt it. The forge-fires jumped a hand higher.
Next time, bring me a feather. I want to see what Heaven makes its generals out of.

choices.text: It came apart into light. There was nothing left.
Next time I will bring you its spear.

lines.label: light
lines.text: Then it was never made of anything at all. Hm. Interesting.

lines.label: spear
lines.text: Hah! Do that and I will forge you something with a Herald's own fire in it.
Pulled a Lancer's spear out of the Plain. Look at the edge.
Folded light. Pretty. But the folds are rushed. Whoever forged this was in a hurry.
Heaven was never in a hurry. Not in ten thousand years. Makes a smith wonder what they are running from.
Eight Forges before mine. Eight smiths. Every one of them swore they could make a blade to kill an Archon.
All eight are slag now. The Court keeps them in a row by the lava, as a warning. Or as decoration.
And you?
Ninth to try. First to be right.
That Choir one sings over my anvil sometimes. Backwards hymns.
Puts a ring in the steel I cannot get any other way. Do not tell her. She will want paying.
Inquisitors now. Judges, they call themselves.
They have burned more of their own this age than of ours. Heaven is turning on itself, Sinbound. And it is turning faster.
Warden. Those chains of yours. My master's master forged the first link, before the god in them went quiet.
It is not quiet. It is listening.
...Keep it away from my anvil.
Ravager. Those horns took the gates of the Silver City. I would pay a hundred souls for one chip of them.
Come and take it.
Hah! Some day. When you are asleep.
Vesper told me. About the chair.
Does not change the work. Steel is still steel.
But I will tell you this, Sinbound. I have always wanted to forge a crown.

lines.label: heavy
lines.text: Heavy. So whoever wears it never forgets what it cost. Good answer.

lines.label: sharp
lines.text: Sharp. So whoever tries to take it bleeds. Better answer.
You came back on your own legs this time. Not through the Font.
Means my steel held. Means you held. Do it again.
Strike while it is hot. Same goes for angels.
Souls in, steel out. Simple.
Mind the sparks. They bite.
A blade is a promise. Make sure yours gets kept.
Font smell is still on you. Go wash in the lava.
Herald-ash on your claws. Suits you.
It is done. The crown. Do not touch it, it is still cooling. It will be cooling for a hundred years.
Iron from the eight dead Forges, one link from the Warden's chains, and a Herald's feather I finally pried out of the ash.
Win the climb, Sinbound, and it is yours. Lose, and I melt it down and try again with the next one. No offence.
Seraph. Your halo would make a fine buckle. Joking. Mostly.
Hexbinder. Keep your ink off my anvil.
Warden. Need those chains re-forged? I will do it for nothing. Do not tell anyone.
Ravager! Butt the anvil again and I butt you back.
Reaper. I keep your scythe's edge in my dreams. It is unsettling.
Hive. Keep your flies off the quench water. Last time the whole batch came out crunchy.
Hive. You came to the forge for steel? You have a sting the length of my forearm.
The sting is for the angels. The steel is for the hive. They like something to build on.
...I will forge you a comb-frame of brimstone. Do not ever tell anyone I made a beehive.
Turncoat. I do not trust a man with two kinds of wing. But I trust your sword arm.
